subject: DPA: private deployment - crypto demarcation and export controls
messages:
From: Anita Gomez <legal@acmehealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-22T08:14:00-07:00
Subject: Clarify DPA for private deployment: key custody & export controls

Marcus / Kimberly —

Thanks for the demo and the Private Deployment overview yesterday. Acme Legal has a handful of focused questions before we can sign the DPA and move to procurement. We tried to collect only privacy- and export-related items; technical/ops questions can go to your infra team. High-level asks below: 

1) Key custody model: the DPA language needs to explicitly state whether Redwood ever has access to customer unwrapped key material for Private deployments (VPC or on-prem). If you do not hold plaintext keys, please confirm the mechanism (customer KMS in VPC, HSM, wrapped keys, etc.).

2) Operator access & break-glass: please describe circumstances where Redwood operators could access customer data or key material, and whether customer approval is required. Can you commit to a contractual clause that requires two-party sign-off for any key export or forensics operation?

3) Subprocessors & onshoring: provide a list of subprocessors (or a mechanism to view the list) and confirm whether any subprocessors are located outside the US. We need to understand geo-export risks and controls.

4) Cross-border transfer/export controls: our compliance team needs to ensure the deployment will not create an uncontrolled export of cryptographic key material or customer content. Any details or constraints helpful here.

We attached a short PDF with the excerpted DPA sections we want to redline (Acme_DPA_Questions.pdf).

Appreciate a quick confirmation — we are hoping to execute by early June. Would prefer written confirmation on the items above; a follow-up call is fine for operational details.

Best,
Anita Gomez
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Acme Healthcare

(attachment: Acme_DPA_Questions.pdf)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Clarify DPA for private deployment: key custody & export controls

Anita —

Thanks for the clear list. Looping in Kimberly (legal) and Karthik (solutions) to make sure we give you both the contractual language and the operational detail. Preliminary answers at a high level:

- For Redwood Private (VPC or on-prem), our standard/configurable option is that customers manage keys in their own KMS/HSM. In that configuration Redwood does not store unwrapped key material.
- We do offer a customer-HSM + key-wrapping option for certain legacy integrations; in that case Redwood only receives wrapped keys and never the raw key bytes.
- Operator access for emergent forensics is handled via documented break-glass runbook and requires explicit customer consent for key unwrap/export; we will provide the runbook and propose contractual language.
- Subprocessor visibility: we can provide a full subprocessors list under NDA; we also publish an aggregated map that shows which roles are US-based vs. offshore.

Attaching a one-page summary for internal ops and the compliance team (redwood_privdep_summary_v1.pdf). We'll follow up with proposed DPA redlines. If helpful I can set a 30-min call with engineering and security tomorrow afternoon.

—Marcus

Hi Anita —

Appreciate the detailed questions. I reviewed with our security and legal ops teams; attached is a short redline that addresses the items you flagged (DPA_redline_proposal.docx). Quick notes: 

- Key custody: we will commit in the DPA that for Customer-managed KMS/HSM models Redwood does not possess or persist unwrapped key material. We propose the following clause: "Redwood will not access, store, or persist Customer unencrypted key material when Customer elects the Customer-managed key option."

- Break-glass/operator access: we cannot promise zero possibility of emergency forensics, but we can guarantee that any operator access that requires the unwrapping or export of key material will be recorded, require prior documented customer approval (email or signed change), and involve at least two Redwood approvers plus the customer approver. We included proposed language.

- Subprocessors: we will provide a subprocessors list via our secure portal (link in email) and agree to a 30-day notice for any new subprocessor. If Acme needs onshore-only subprocessors we can propose an onshoring schedule and identify roles that can be localized.

- Cross-border transfer: our Private deployment modes are designed to keep customer content and keys inside the customer's VPC region. Where transient telemetry or logs are shipped for support, we can provide options to disable or encrypt telemetry and to push logs to customer-owned endpoints.

I'm attaching the redline and a sanitized subprocessors summary. If you are comfortable, Marcus and I can jump on a call with your compliance team tomorrow to run the proposed language live.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park

Subject: Re: Clarify DPA for private deployment: key custody & export controls

Anita —

Thanks — here are concise confirmations and a proposed next step: 

1) Customer key custody models (Private deployments)
   - Customer-managed KMS/HSM (recommended): customer injects keys into their KMS/HSM in the VPC or on-prem environment. Redwood never receives unwrapped key material. Keys are referenced by API but are never exported to Redwood infrastructure.
   - Customer-HSM + key-wrapping: customer performs initial key generation or loading into HSM; Redwood receives only wrapped key blobs for use in the runtime. We never receive plaintext keys.

2) Operator access & break-glass
   - Any operation that would result in unwrapping or export of key material requires:
     a) written authorization from an Acme security lead (email or DocuSign), and
     b) two authorized Redwood approvers (one engineering lead + one security engineer).
   - All such events are recorded in an immutable audit trail (we push a copy of the audit events to the customer's logging endpoint and retain our own tamper-evident record). We are prepared to add explicit contractual language and an appendix listing the audit fields and retention windows.

3) Subprocessors & geography
   - The current support/telemetry subprocessors include a small number of third parties for log storage and ticketing; two roles (support escalation and telemetry parsing) are performed by teams in the EU and India. We can offer an onshoring plan for Acme (timeline ~60 days) or revised controls to ensure no key material or decrypted content leaves the US. Subprocessor details available under NDA: https://redwood.ai/nda/subprocessors/ACME

4) Cross-border transfers
   - Private Deployments keep customer content and keys within the nominated region by design. Any telemetry/export that could include customer content is configurable and can be disabled or encrypted to a customer-managed endpoint.

Attachments: operator_breakglass_runbook.pdf — this is the operational playbook that defines the approval flow, required artifacts, and the audit trail fields. Link to runbook (internal): https://redwood.ai/links/privdep-runbook-789

Next step: propose a 30-min call tomorrow (May 24) at 10:00am PT with Acme security, Kimberly, Olga (security ops), and Karthik (solutions) to agree final DPA redlines and sign-off path. If that works, Marcus will send a calendar invite and a short agenda.

Thanks,
